title: The worm stays cut

data.source: 200 trials of 4000 occasions: a slowly wandering truth seen through noise, followed by the seed rule of Phoenix_Egg/CORE/MATHEMATICS.md (R5) and by a variant that is wiped every 7th occasion. Seeded; the lens's own trials.
data.licence: none needed (generated here from a seed)

prediction: Plain R5 keeps an injury above one part in a thousand for 44 occasions (J0); a seed wiped every 7th occasion keeps it at most 7 (J1); and the wiped seed follows a slowly changing truth with no more than twice plain R5's mean square error (J2).
baseline: Plain R5; the steady Kalman filter, which is the same recursion with the best q; and two decoys, remembering nothing and believing only the last occasion.
why: The variant fails, against plain R5. Wiping the seed every seventh occasion does shorten how long one injury lingers, from 44 occasions to 7. But it throws away everything else the seed had learned, and the seed then follows a slowly changing truth far worse, worse even than believing only the last occasion. Forgetting is the only release this equation can offer, and forgetting is a poor trade. It is the museum's variant that fails here, not the owner's CRR.
claim_kind: engineering usefulness (of a museum variant, against CRR as given)

alternatives.forks: 12 settings (jubilee every 3, 7, 12, 49; q 0.8, 0.9, 0.95) in two worlds. J2 held in 0 of 12 when the truth wanders off, and in 10 of 12 when it keeps returning to the prior.

operating_characteristics: The outcome follows from the two recursions and the world they are put in. It can show a variant is useless; it cannot weigh on CRR.
second_check: Adapted and re-run by a worker who did not write the mapping. No person has reviewed it.
variants: V-spiritual-2 (the jubilee seed; museum experiment, not the owner's CRR)
